text:
**A 200 W panel refills 1,000 Wh in about 1.5 days of decent sun. A 300-400 W setup can do it in one day.**

**The math**

Panel watts ≈ capacity ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle, and charging losses. [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge) and [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/) use 0.75, and [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/) uses 0.7.

For a full recharge from empty in one day, the panel wattage needed for 1,000 Wh is ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)):

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts |
|---|---|
| 3 | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 | ~270 W |
| 6 | ~230 W |

**If you can wait longer**

- A common rule of thumb is battery Wh ÷ 5, so about 200 W for a day and a half of decent sun ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- At 4.5 sun hours and 70% efficiency, a 200 W panel gives ~630 Wh/day. A 400 W panel gives ~1,260 Wh/day, enough to fill the station in under a day. A 100 W panel takes about 3 days.
- Winter changes this a lot. In a northern January with about 2 peak sun hours, a one-day recharge needs roughly 700 W ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

**Check your station before buying panels**

- **Max solar input (watts):** a station that accepts only 200 W won't use a 400 W panel's extra output.
- **Input voltage window:** the panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside it. Going over can damage the charge controller, and wiring panels in series adds their voltages ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Connectors:** confirm the adapter cable you need is included.
- **Running loads while charging:** this slows the net recharge.

**One option if you want 400 W**

The [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel) is listed at $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26 (the listing says the code expires 2026-12-30). That link is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you.

- Its Voc is 45.3 V, which suits stations that accept 12-60 V solar input.
- It's heavy at 18.5 kg.
- It's too high-voltage for some small stations, so check your station's input range first.
